# The Anima and Animus

Every man carries within him the eternal image of woman, not the image of this or that particular woman, but a definite feminine image. This image is fundamentally unconscious, an hereditary factor of primordial origin engraved in the living organic system of the man, an imprint or archetype of all the ancestral experiences of the female. The anima is the archetype of life itself.

Since this image is unconscious, it is always unconsciously projected upon the person of the beloved, and is one of the chief reasons for passionate attraction or aversion. The anima represents the contrasexual element in a man's psyche; correspondingly, the animus represents the masculine element in a woman's psyche. These soul images function as bridges to the unconscious.

The animus in woman corresponds to the paternal Logos just as the anima in man corresponds to the maternal Eros. The animus is the deposit of all woman's ancestral experiences of man — and not only that, he is also a creative and procreative being. The natural function of the animus and anima is to serve as a bridge between individual consciousness and the collective unconscious.

When the anima or animus is projected onto another person, it creates a peculiar fascination or repulsion that has little to do with the actual qualities of the other. Withdrawing these projections through conscious reflection is one of the most difficult yet essential tasks of psychological development. The integration of the contrasexual archetype leads to a deeper understanding of oneself and of human relationships.
